decision: Observe original Rust callback Vec capacity across Bytes aliases separately from logical queue bytes and conservative reservation. HTTP/2 DATA consumes passive observed credit; opposite-direction connection WINDOW_UPDATE grants it. Snapshot reads do not fabricate credit release. Use existing pinned limits; full platform receive-memory qualification remains required.

sections: Browser resource proof and feasibility result
source_decisions.basis: Byte/item bounds, consumption-based flow credit, conservative connection envelope; WebSocket bufferedAmount measures outbound backlog only. Browser engine receive allocation before callback must be physically qualified.
Vec::capacity is retained through Bytes aliases; final backing drop frees original Vec before capacity release. Passive credit facts and conservative reservation remain separate observables.
Actual Uint8Array.to_vec calls the same canonical Rust allocation owner after the engine has allocated callback input.

bounded_example.expected: Actual Vec capacity is measured dynamically and retained until final alias drop even when logical queue is empty/closed; no zero capacity is inferred from partial reads or empty queue.
